Hi Sophie / Alex —

Thanks for taking the call earlier — excited to partner on the MAP and pilot for Nimbus's conversational assistant. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP-v1.docx) and a concise perf-eval outline. High level we propose:

- MAP milestones: pilot infra (worth 2 weeks), eval window (3 business days of sustained load), rollout gating (SLA, perf, and cost thresholds).
- Eval goals: characterize TTFT (time-to-first-token), P50/P95 token latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency scaling across GPUs.
- Hardware matrix: A100 80GB (full GPU), H100 80GB, L40S 48GB — test full-GPU and representative MIG splits (A100 2x1g/3g, H100 7g/1g etc) to show economics at scale.

We want to run two representative workloads:
1) Short-turn chat (seq_len=128, avg_resp=40 tokens) — latency-sensitive, concurrency target 8–16
2) Long-form generation (seq_len=1024, avg_resp=300 tokens) — throughput-focused, concurrency 2–4

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0: sign MAP and confirm dataset/prompt corpus (you provide redlines + security checklist)
- Week 1: infra provisioning + baseline tests
- Week 2: deep benchmarking, cost modeling, and recommendation doc

Can you confirm the dataset (sample prompts) and whether the pilot must run in us-west-2? Also flag any hard latency SLOs (e.g., TTFT < 200ms P95).

Related attachments: MAP-v1.docx (deliverables + approvals).

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom / team —

Draft of the technical evaluation plan (high-level):

1) Test harness and workloads
- Use JMeter + custom token streamer to reproduce client burst patterns.
- Short-turn (seq=128): 10k requests across 3 sustained intervals, concurrency sweep [2,4,8,12,16].
- Long-form (seq=1024): 2k requests, concurrency [1,2,4].

2) Models and runtimes
- Model: open-llama-70b-f32 + quantized variants we plan to serve.
- Runtimes: our optimized runtime with kernel selection; test with quantization profiles enabled/disabled.

3) GPU matrix
- Full: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB (single GPU instance each).
- MIG variants: split A100 as 2x1g/3g; H100 attempt 7g/1g or vendor-specified partitions.

4) Metrics to capture
- TTFT (measured client-side), token P50/P95 latency, end-to-end response time, tokens/sec sustained, GPU utilization, memory headroom, and cost-per-1k-tokens (raw infra cost + model licensing as applicable).

5) Artifacts and deliverables
- benchmark-results.csv (per-run logs), perf-plot PDFs, short recommendation memo (nimbus-benchmark-summary.pdf).

6) Acceptance criteria (for rollout recommendation)
- Short-turn: P95 TTFT <= 250ms and cost per 1k tokens within 1.8x of current baseline.
- Long-form: sustained tokens/sec sufficient to meet 95th percentile throughput target and CPU/GPU thermal headroom > 10% on average.

I'll attach the harness config and expected command lines. Plan to run the matrix in us-west-2 on Tuesday (Week 2).

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

Subject: Results: Nimbus pilot benchmark summary (A100 vs H100 vs L40S)

Hi Sophie / Alex —

We completed the three-day eval window and attached the summary + raw results. Key findings (executive summary):

Short-turn chat (seq=128, avg_resp=40 tokens, concurrency experiments):
- A100 (full 80GB): P50 TTFT 62 ms, P95 TTFT 210 ms, sustained throughput ~170 tok/s @ concurrency 8; MIG 1g partitions drop throughput by ~55% and increase P95 by ~40 ms.
- H100 (full 80GB): P50 TTFT 48 ms, P95 TTFT 165 ms, sustained throughput ~240 tok/s @ concurrency 8; MIG partitions on H100 retained ~70% throughput vs full.
- L40S (48GB): P50 TTFT 75 ms, P95 TTFT 260 ms, sustained throughput ~120 tok/s; best cost per token on embedding and low-concurrency workloads, weaker at high-concurrency gen.

Long-form generation (seq=1024, avg_resp=300 tokens):
- A100: average token latency 18–22 ms/token; end-to-end avg response 3.6s at concurrency 2; thermal throttling observed on 12h runs (GPU mem pressure).
- H100: 12–16 ms/token; end-to-end avg response 2.8s; better kernel throughput and less mem pressure for fused attention in our runtime.

Cost model (ballpark, infra only):
- H100 per-token infra cost ~1.25x A100 for short-turn but H100 cost per successful request lower when you include reduced retry/remediation due to lower TTFT.
- L40S cost per token ~0.65x A100 but requires more instances for concurrency-heavy patterns, which increases ops complexity.

MIG takeaways:
- MIG on A100 shows significant fragmentation overhead for generation workloads; recommended only for low-latency, ultra-low-cost inference for small models.
- H100 MIG offers better isolation with lower penalty; for Nimbus's mixed workload we recommend 1–2 H100 full GPUs for prod frontends + L40S nodes for background batch/embedding jobs.

Recommendations:
1) Pilot → Prod path: Use 2x H100 full GPUs behind our smart routing for low-latency frontends, scale L40S fleet for bulk batch/embedding.
2) Reserve capacity (Dedicated) for top traffic tier; confirm committed throughput to model provisioning in the MAP.
3) Next steps: finalize MAP sign-off, procurement SOW, and DocuSign for reserved capacity pricing (I dropped links below).

I've attached Nimbus-benchmark-summary.pdf (4 pages) and the raw CSVs (benchmark-results.csv) for your engineers. Happy to walk through numbers live; propose Wed 11/3 at 10am PT for handoff.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
